text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
CATHERINE II, who gained the throne of Russia after her husband was murdered, was born in 1729.
The Austrian journalist THEODOR HERZL, who advocated the idea of a Jewish state, was born in 1860. He became the first president of the World Zionist Organisation in 1897.
The "Red Baron" BARON MANFRED VON RICHTHOFEN was born in 1892. He was a German airforce officer who was noted for his dogfights in World War I.
American paediatrician DR BENJAMIN SPOCK was born in 1903. His books influenced a generation of parents into non-violent parenting methods.

American singer and actor BING COSBY was born in 1904. He had the biggest-selling single ever with "White Christmas". The estimated sales range from 30 to more than 130 million. He was considered to be the most popular artist of the first half of the 20th century. During 30 years he accumulated more than 340 hits, 23 of them with the Andrews Sisters. He had 16 million sellers and 40 number ones in USA. BING also starred in more than 50 films. He died in Madrid on 14th October, 1977.

UK singer ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK (ARNOLD GEORGE DORSEY) was born in 1936. His first records were released in his own name but success came after TOM JONES' manager renamed him after the German composer. Hits included "Release Me" (1967), "The Last Waltz" (1967) and "After The Lovin'" (1976).
The girl who was discovered while singing in a Manhattan hotel, LESLEY GORE, was born in 1946. Her biggest hits were with "It's My Party" (1963) and "You Don't Own Me" (1963).
US bass player with The Knack PRESCOTT NILES was born in 1954.
**EVENTS**
1519 : The Florentine painter LEONARDO DA VINCI died in
France at the age of 67.
1670 : The Hudson's Bay Company was chartered by the
English crown and given a monopoly of the trade into Hudson Bay, Canada.
1900 : A bill was passed in the US Congress for the
building of the Nicaraguan Canal.
1925 : A US navy seaplane set a record by remaining in
the air for 28.5 hours.
1926 : Indian women were allowed to run for public office
for the first time.
1933 : ADOLF HITLER banned trade unions.
1945 : All one million German troops in Italy and Austria
surrender.
1965 : The first satellite television progamme linked
nine countries and more than 300 million viewers.
1972 : The head of the FBI, J.EDGAR HOOVER, died.
1980 : A British pop song was banned in South Africa

after being used as an unofficial anthem for anti-racists. Pink Floyd's hit "Another Brick In The Wall" was taken up by black school children to highlight the discrimination within the education system which spent six times as much educating a white child as a black child. The young protesters chanted the lines of the song that had meaning for them -"We don't want no education, we don't want no thought control".
1982 : In the Falklands war, the Argentine cruiser
General Belgrano was sunk by the British submarine Conqueror; over 350 men were killed.
1989 : China imposed martial law as pro-democracy
demonstrators camped in Tienanmen Square.
1994 : President F.W. de KLERK conceded victory to NELSON
MANDELA in the country's historic all-race elections.
1995 : Serb missiles exploded in the heart of Zagreb,
killing six people.
